summary: Persistent memory for coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI, so decisions and fixes from past sessions can be recalled later.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: agentmemory records your coding-agent sessions, makes decisions and fixes searchable and lets agents recall them later. It works with Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Hermes, OpenClaw, OpenCode and any MCP client, and keeps one memory store across all of them with a live viewer to browse and edit it.
sixtySeconds.problem: Coding agents forget everything between sessions and between tools. agentmemory keeps project history, lessons and handoffs so the next session or agent can pick them up.
whoFor: Developers using one or more coding agents
People who want inspectable agent memory
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for one shared memory across many agents, keyword search that works without an API key, and a viewer to inspect and forget memories.
requirements: curl, sh and tar on macOS/Linux
Windows: WSL2 or the native Windows setup

overview: Run the setup command, choose your agents and either a model provider or keyless mode. Setup writes the config, starts the memory server and offers a global install of the agentmemory command.
The API runs at localhost:3111 and the viewer at localhost:3113, both bound to loopback. Keyless mode uses keyword (BM25) search; adding an embedding provider enables semantic search.
Hooks and plugins capture session events with secret scrubbing. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
